# Current Nix and NixOS

**Goal:** Know which Nix and which NixOS this book means by "current" on 13 November 2026, and which number you are allowed to bump later.

Three different clocks get called "the version":

| Clock | What moves it | What you type |
|-------|----------------|---------------|
| Nix, the program | The Nix release | `nix --version` |
| nixpkgs branch | Release managers, then your lock | `github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05` |
| `system.stateVersion` | You, once, at install | `"26.05"` and then you stop |

A host can run Nix 2.35.3 from nixpkgs (or 2.35.6 from the upstream installer), evaluate nixpkgs 26.05, and still carry `system.stateVersion = "25.11"` from the day it was installed. All three are correct at once.

## Nix 2.35.6

The current stable Nix tag is **2.35.6**, tagged 10 November 2026. The 2.35 line opened in mid-2026 (2.35.0). Patch releases since then are fixes on that line. There is no 2.36 stable tag. On the `nixos-26.05` tip, `nixVersions.git` is a 2.36 pre-release snapshot. Leave it off the lab.

Features from 2.35 that change daily work:

| Area | What you do with it |
|------|---------------------|
| Flake sources | Nix copies flake files into the store lazily. A file the evaluation never reads is not part of the eval hash. |
| HTTP/3 | Off unless you set `http3 = true` in `nix.conf` or pass `--http3`. Leave it off until a fetch fails in a way you have measured. |
| FreeBSD | The FreeBSD build can sandbox with jails. Linux sandbox behaviour is unchanged. |
| Allocator | The `nix` binary links mimalloc for non-GC allocations. You do not configure this. |

Stock NixOS 26.05 uses `nixVersions.stable`. On the 26.05 tip checked with this chapter, that attribute is **2.34.9**, so `nix --version` prints a 2.34 line until you override it. The 26.11 draft notes are the first NixOS branch that moves the channel Nix to 2.35.

`nixVersions.nix_2_35` exists on 26.05, and `nixVersions.latest` points at it. The package version follows the nixpkgs commit, not the newest upstream tag. On this same tip the attribute is **2.35.3**, not 2.35.6. A later lock of `nixos-26.05` may bump the patch. Set the attribute when you want the 2.35 line:

```nix
{ pkgs, ... }:
{
  nix.package = pkgs.nixVersions.nix_2_35;
}
```

Confirm after the rebuild:

```bash
nix --version
```

A 2.35 line means the option applied. The patch number is the one in your lock (2.35.3 on the tip above). A 2.34 line means you are still on `nixVersions.stable`, or you booted a generation from before the rebuild.

Foreign Linux (the Fedora path in this book) gets Nix from the upstream installer, which tracks the current stable tag. The 10 November 2026 installer is 2.35.6. That number and the NixOS package number are allowed to differ by a few patches.

## NixOS 26.05 "Yarara"

26.05 is the stable release you install today.

| Fact | Value |
|------|--------|
| Released | 30 May 2026 |
| Support | Bugfixes and security updates through 31 December 2026 |
| Previous stable | 25.11 "Xantusia", end of life 30 June 2026 |
| Next stable | 26.11 "Zokor", scheduled, not released |
| Initrd | systemd stage 1 is the default. The scripted initrd is deprecated. |
| Desktop ISO | GNOME 50 |
| Compiler | GCC 15. LLVM stays at 21. |
| Darwin | Last nixpkgs release that builds `x86_64-darwin`. That platform is dropped for 26.11. |

The release was 59,703 commits from 2,842 contributors: about 20,442 packages added, 20,641 updated, 17,532 removed, plus 85 new NixOS modules. Those counts are the size of the branch, not a list you need to read. Read the release notes for modules you actually enable. The internals chapter on reading release notes is the method.

Pin the branch, then let the lock pick the commit:

```nix
{
  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05";
}
```

```bash
nix flake metadata
nix flake update nixpkgs
```

`nixos-26.05` moves when Hydra's tested job is green. `flake.lock` does not move until you update it. Commit the lock in the same change as the rebuild that survived.

## NixOS 26.11 "Zokor" is not the pin yet

Release managers scheduled 26.11 for 30 November 2026. The date moved from 23 November because the staging cycle was long, and the schedule says it can still slip. Branch-off of `staging` was estimated for 14 November 2026, inside the current staging cycle, with a single staging cycle before the release branch. The Zero Hydra Failures campaign for 26.11 opened on 7 November 2026 and runs until the release.

Until the release announcement exists, new lab hosts stay on `nixos-26.05`. `nixos-unstable` is a tested rolling channel. It is the wrong accident to land in because a helper flag wrote it for you. It is a reasonable second input when a tool is only packaged there, named as its own input, with `follows` left off on purpose.

Draft notes already on `master` for 26.11, useful so the upgrade runbook is not a surprise:

| Draft note | What it means on a machine you already installed |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Channel Nix becomes 2.35 | The `nix.package` pin above may become redundant. Check `nix --version` after the bump before you delete it. |
| GNOME 51 | Matters if you enable GNOME. Plasma is a separate module. |
| PostgreSQL 18 for `stateVersion >= "26.11"` | New installs pick 18. An existing data directory stays on the version its `stateVersion` selected. Do not bump `stateVersion` to "match the release". |
| `nixexprs.tar.xz` retired with 27.05 after 31 December 2027 | Channel-tarball inputs should use `.tar.zst`. |
| Scripted stage 1 scheduled for removal | 26.05 already defaults to systemd stage 1. A host that still sets the scripted initrd needs a boot test before 26.11. |

When 26.11 is announced, the upgrade is: change `26.05` to `26.11` in the input, `nix flake update nixpkgs`, eval, build, boot a lab generation, read the final release notes. `system.stateVersion` stays `"26.05"` on this lab.

## What to trust when a page disagrees

| Source | Use it for |
|--------|------------|
| [NixOS 26.05 announcement](https://nixos.org/blog/announcements/2026/nixos-2605/) | Support dates, headline changes |
| NixOS and nixpkgs release notes for 26.05 | Options you must change |
| [status.nixos.org](https://status.nixos.org/) | Whether `nixos-26.05` and `nixos-unstable` have moved, and whether the tested job is red |
| `nix --version` and `flake.lock` | What this machine actually runs |
| A draft 26.11 note on `master` | A forecast. The released note wins later. |

```bash
curl -fsS https://channels.nixos.org/nixos-26.05/git-revision
nix flake metadata github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05
```

The first command is the commit the channel is serving. The second is the commit your flake would lock if you updated now. They match when you just updated. They diverge on purpose between updates.

## The boring rule

- Install and pin **26.05** until 26.11 is released and the lab has a written bump.
- CLI baseline is the **2.35 line**. Upstream tag **2.35.6** (10 November 2026). On NixOS 26.05, `nix.package = pkgs.nixVersions.nix_2_35` (2.35.3 on the tip checked here). Stock remains 2.34.9 until you set that.
- `system.stateVersion` is the install release. It is not a badge you refresh.
- 25.11 is for reading old machines. Its security updates have stopped.
- `x86_64-darwin` work ends with 26.05. New Darwin pins are `aarch64-darwin`.
